questions.prompt: Which word is a proper noun in the sentence: Njeri visited Kisumu in April?
questions.correctAnswer: Kisumu
questions.explanation: Kisumu names a specific place, so it begins with a capital letter as a proper noun.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify proper nouns in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adjective in the sentence: The careful pupil packed the books?
questions.correctAnswer: careful
questions.explanation: Careful describes the pupil, so it is an adjective.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize adjectives that describe nouns.

questions.prompt: Which word is a verb in the sentence: The choir sang beautifully during assembly?
questions.correctAnswer: sang
questions.explanation: Sang shows the action done by the choir.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify action verbs in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end the sentence: Where is my exercise book
questions.correctAnswer: question mark
questions.explanation: The sentence asks a direct question, so it should end with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Use punctuation marks to end different sentence types.

questions.prompt: Which word means nearly the same as happy?
questions.correctAnswer: joyful
questions.explanation: Joyful and happy both describe a feeling of pleasure.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify synonyms of common words.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of polite?
questions.correctAnswer: rude
questions.explanation: Rude is the opposite of polite because it means not showing good manners.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify antonyms of familiar words.

questions.prompt: Which option is a polite way to ask for a pencil?
options: May I borrow your pencil, please?
questions.correctAnswer: May I borrow your pencil, please?
questions.explanation: The words may I and please make the request polite.
questions.learningOutcome: Use courteous expressions in everyday conversations.

questions.prompt: Which greeting is suitable when meeting your teacher at 8 o'clock in the morning?
questions.correctAnswer: Good morning
questions.explanation: Good morning is used as a greeting during the morning hours.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose greetings that fit time and situation.

questions.prompt: Which option is written in plural form?
questions.correctAnswer: children
questions.explanation: Children means more than one child.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize plural forms of common nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop?
questions.correctAnswer: The lesson is over.
questions.explanation: A statement begins with a capital letter and usually ends with a full stop.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic capitalization and punctuation in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in the sentence: The athlete ran quickly?
questions.correctAnswer: quickly
questions.explanation: Quickly tells how the athlete ran, so it is an adverb.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that describe actions.

questions.prompt: Which word is a pronoun in the sentence: They cleaned the classroom?
questions.correctAnswer: They
questions.explanation: They is used in place of the names of people.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personal pronouns in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which option names a person, place, animal, or thing?
questions.correctAnswer: noun
questions.explanation: A noun names a person, place, animal, or thing.
questions.learningOutcome: State the function of common parts of speech.

questions.prompt: Which word joins the two ideas in this sentence: I wanted tea but the flask was empty?
questions.correctAnswer: but
questions.explanation: But is a conjunction that joins contrasting ideas.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize conjunctions used to join ideas.

questions.prompt: Which item would most likely appear first in a dictionary entry?
questions.correctAnswer: the word being defined
questions.explanation: A dictionary entry begins with the word whose meaning is being explained.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic parts of a dictionary entry.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct subject-verb agreement.
options: The girls play netball after school.
The girls plays netball after school.
The girls playing netball after school.
The girls has play netball after school.
questions.correctAnswer: The girls play netball after school.
questions.explanation: A plural subject such as girls takes the verb play in the simple present tense.
questions.learningOutcome: Use verbs that agree with singular and plural subjects.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct past tense form: Yesterday, Otieno ____ a letter to his aunt.
questions.correctAnswer: wrote
questions.explanation: Wrote is the past tense form of write.
questions.learningOutcome: Use past tense forms of common verbs correctly.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct future tense form: Tomorrow, the class ____ the museum.
questions.correctAnswer: will visit
questions.explanation: Will visit shows an action that is expected to happen in the future.
questions.learningOutcome: Use future tense forms in meaningful sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly to show ownership?
questions.correctAnswer: Amina's bag is blue.
questions.explanation: The apostrophe and s show that the bag belongs to Amina.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apostrophes to show possession in simple phrases.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a comma correctly in a list?
options: We carried books, pencils, rulers and crayons.
We carried books pencils rulers and crayons.
We carried, books pencils rulers and crayons.
We carried books pencils, rulers and crayons.
questions.correctAnswer: We carried books, pencils, rulers and crayons.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a list so the reader can follow them easily.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas to separate items in a list.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: The dog wagged ____ tail.
questions.correctAnswer: its
questions.explanation: Its is used for something belonging to an animal or thing when gender is not the focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable possessive pronouns in context.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses an adverb of manner.
questions.correctAnswer: The scout spoke clearly.
questions.explanation: Clearly tells how the scout spoke, so it is an adverb of manner.
questions.learningOutcome: Use adverbs of manner to describe actions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the preposition correctly?
options: The key is under the mat.
The key is quickly the mat.
The key is happy the mat.
The key is because the mat.
questions.correctAnswer: The key is under the mat.
questions.explanation: Under shows the position of the key in relation to the mat.
questions.learningOutcome: Use prepositions to show position.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the present continuous tense?
options: The learners read silently every day.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners are reading silently.
questions.explanation: Are reading shows an action happening now.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize present continuous tense in sentences.

questions.prompt: Read the sentence: The road was slippery after the rain. What does slippery mean?
options: hard to walk on without sliding
questions.correctAnswer: hard to walk on without sliding
questions.explanation: A slippery surface can make people slide or fall, especially after rain.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer the meaning of words from sentence context.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same vowel sound as the word seat?
questions.correctAnswer: bean
questions.explanation: Seat and bean both have the long ee sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish similar vowel sounds in spoken words.

questions.prompt: Which pair of words are homophones?
questions.correctAnswer: flour and flower
questions.explanation: Flour and flower sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize homophones in familiar vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows a command?
questions.correctAnswer: Close the door gently.
questions.explanation: A command tells someone to do something.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify commands among different sentence types.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows an exclamation?
questions.correctAnswer: What a beautiful mural!
questions.explanation: An exclamation shows strong feeling and often ends with an exclamation mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify exclamatory sentences and their punctuation.

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the comparison: This bag is ____ than that one.
questions.correctAnswer: heavier
questions.explanation: Heavier compares two things.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparative adjectives correctly.

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the comparison: Of all the runners, Wanjiku was the ____.
questions.correctAnswer: fastest
questions.explanation: Fastest compares one runner with all the others in the group.
questions.learningOutcome: Use superlative adjectives correctly.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly completes the sentence: Neither the captain nor the players ____ late.
questions.correctAnswer: were
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer plural noun players, so were is suitable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply subject-verb agreement in sentences with compound subjects.

questions.prompt: Which phrase would best begin a friendly letter to your cousin?
questions.correctAnswer: Dear Brian,
questions.explanation: A friendly letter usually begins with Dear followed by the person's name.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify parts of an informal letter.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
options: Please sit down, said the teacher.
Please sit down," said the teacher.
questions.correctAnswer: "Please sit down," said the teacher.
questions.explanation: Quotation marks enclose the exact words spoken.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate direct speech in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence correctly: We walked ____ the library after lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: to
questions.explanation: To shows direction toward the library.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose correct words based on meaning and use.

questions.prompt: Which option best completes the sentence: The class planted trees ____ the school compound would be greener.
questions.correctAnswer: so that
questions.explanation: So that introduces the purpose of planting the trees.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to show reason and purpose.

questions.prompt: Which title would best fit a paragraph about washing hands before eating?
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping Germs Away
questions.explanation: Washing hands before eating helps prevent germs, so the title matches the main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable titles that match short texts.

questions.prompt: Read the sentence: The pupils whispered because the baby was asleep. Why did the pupils whisper?
options: They did not want to wake the baby.
questions.correctAnswer: They did not want to wake the baby.
questions.explanation: The reason is shown by the phrase because the baby was asleep.
questions.learningOutcome: Answer direct comprehension questions from a sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about school clubs?
options: School clubs help learners discover their talents.
The bell rang at four o'clock.
I put my book in the desk.
questions.correctAnswer: School clubs help learners discover their talents.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose topic sentences that introduce a clear main idea.

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence: There are many ____ on the shelf.
questions.correctAnswer: books
questions.explanation: Many shows more than one, so the plural noun books is needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Use regular plural nouns in sentences.

questions.prompt: Read the passage: Moraa arrived at school early. She swept the reading corner and arranged the storybooks before the bell rang. What can you tell about Moraa?
questions.correctAnswer: She is responsible.
questions.explanation: Moraa helped care for the classroom before lessons began, which shows responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer a character trait from actions in a short text.

questions.prompt: Read the passage: The sky turned dark, and a cold wind shook the banana leaves. Father asked us to bring the clothes inside. What would most likely happen next?
options: The clothes would dry faster outside.
questions.correctAnswer: It would rain.
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and cold wind often show that rain is coming.
questions.learningOutcome: Make logical predictions using clues in a short passage.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly combines these ideas: I was tired. I finished my homework.
options: Although I was tired, I finished my homework.
I was tired because I finished my homework although.
Finished my homework I was tired.
I was tired but because homework.
questions.correctAnswer: Although I was tired, I finished my homework.
questions.explanation: Although joins two contrasting ideas in a clear sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine ideas using suitable conjunctions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly changes the direct speech to reported speech: "I am ready," said Halima.
options: Halima said that she was ready.
Halima said that I am ready.
Halima said that she is ready yesterday.
questions.correctAnswer: Halima said that she was ready.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, I changes to she and am changes to was.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple direct speech into reported speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly changes the reported speech to direct speech: Kamau said that he liked reading.
questions.correctAnswer: Kamau said, "I like reading."
questions.explanation: Direct speech gives Kamau's exact words, so he becomes I.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple reported speech into direct speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
options: The girl who won the race is my desk mate.
The girl which won the race is my desk mate.
The girl when won the race is my desk mate.
The girl because won the race is my desk mate.
questions.correctAnswer: The girl who won the race is my desk mate.
questions.explanation: Who is used to refer to a person.
questions.learningOutcome: Use relative pronouns to add information about nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in passive voice?
options: The door was opened by the monitor.
The monitor is opening the door.
The monitor will open the door.
questions.correctAnswer: The door was opened by the monitor.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the receiver of the action comes before the doer.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize active and passive voice in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence changes this active sentence into passive voice: The chef prepared the meal.
options: The meal was prepared by the chef.
The chef was prepared by the meal.
The chef is preparing the meal.
questions.correctAnswer: The meal was prepared by the chef.
questions.explanation: The object meal becomes the subject, and was prepared shows passive voice.
questions.learningOutcome: Transform simple active sentences into passive voice.

questions.prompt: Which option best completes the sentence: If we leave early, we ____ the bus.
questions.correctAnswer: will catch
questions.explanation: Will catch fits a likely future result after the condition if we leave early.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple conditional sentences to show likely results.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a simile?
options: The hall was as quiet as a library.
The hall is a big box.
questions.correctAnswer: The hall was as quiet as a library.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using like or as.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify similes in simple literary sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
options: The wind whispered through the trees.
The wind came from the east.
questions.correctAnswer: The wind whispered through the trees.
questions.explanation: Personification gives human actions to something that is not human.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personification in literary texts.

questions.prompt: Which line has alliteration?
questions.correctAnswer: Brave Brian baked brown bread.
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the same beginning sound in nearby words.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize sound patterns in poems and chants.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains the proverb: A stitch in time saves nine?
options: Solving a small problem early prevents a bigger one.
Sewing is always easier at night.
Nine stitches are better than one.
Time can be stored in a basket.
questions.correctAnswer: Solving a small problem early prevents a bigger one.
questions.explanation: The proverb teaches that early action can prevent more trouble later.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common proverbs and sayings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the idiom pull up your socks correctly?
options: After missing practice, the coach told us to pull up our socks.
I pulled up my socks because they were blue.
The socks pulled up the coach.
We pulled up the socks into the cupboard.
questions.correctAnswer: After missing practice, the coach told us to pull up our socks.
questions.explanation: The idiom means to improve one's effort or behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common idioms according to meaning and context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct order of adjectives?
options: She bought three small red baskets.
She bought red three small baskets.
She bought small three red baskets.
She bought baskets three small red.
questions.correctAnswer: She bought three small red baskets.
questions.explanation: Number usually comes before size and colour when several adjectives describe a noun.
questions.learningOutcome: Order adjectives naturally in noun phrases.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect tense correctly?
options: The learners have finished the project.
The learners has finished the project.
The learners have finish the project.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners have finished the project.
questions.explanation: Have finished is the present perfect form for a plural subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Use present perfect tense with suitable helping verbs.

questions.prompt: Which option completes the sentence with a suitable question tag: You are coming for practice, ____?
questions.correctAnswer: aren't you
questions.explanation: A positive statement usually takes a negative question tag with the same helping verb.
questions.learningOutcome: Use question tags correctly in everyday speech.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly completes the sentence: The books on the desk ____ mine.
questions.correctAnswer: are
questions.explanation: Books is plural, so the verb are agrees with it.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply subject-verb agreement when extra words follow the subject.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph order makes the most sense for giving directions to the library?
options: Start at the gate, turn left at the office, then walk to the blue door.
Walk to the blue door, start at the gate, then turn left at the office.
Turn left at the office, finish reading, then start at the gate.
Start at the gate, close the book, then ask about lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: Start at the gate, turn left at the office, then walk to the blue door.
questions.explanation: Directions should follow the order a person will move from the starting point to the destination.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange instructions in a logical order.

questions.prompt: Which closing is most suitable for a friendly letter to your friend?
questions.correctAnswer: Your friend, Achieng
questions.explanation: A friendly letter can close warmly using words such as Your friend.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable closings for informal letters.

questions.prompt: Which detail would be most important in a notice about a school clean-up day?
options: date, time, place and what to bring
questions.correctAnswer: date, time, place and what to bring
questions.explanation: A notice should give clear details that help readers know what to do.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key details needed in public notices.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best summary of this sentence: The pupils collected litter, swept the paths and watered the flowers during environment club.
options: The pupils cleaned and cared for the school compound.
The pupils watched a football match.
questions.correctAnswer: The pupils cleaned and cared for the school compound.
questions.explanation: A summary gives the main idea without listing every small action.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarize main ideas from short texts.

questions.prompt: Which word has the prefix in the sentence: The team will repaint the classroom walls?
questions.correctAnswer: repaint
questions.explanation: The prefix re- is added to paint to form repaint, meaning paint again.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify prefixes and explain how they change word meaning.

questions.prompt: Which word has a suffix that means full of?
questions.correctAnswer: hopeful
questions.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of, so hopeful means full of hope.
questions.learningOutcome: Use suffixes to understand word meanings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses there, their, or they're correctly?
options: Their classroom is near the office.
There classroom is near the office.
They're classroom is near the office.
Theyre classroom is near the office.
questions.correctAnswer: Their classroom is near the office.
questions.explanation: Their shows possession, so it fits before classroom.
questions.learningOutcome: Select correct homophones based on meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correctly punctuated as a direct question?
options: Why did the bus stop near the gate?
Why did the bus stop near the gate.
Why did the bus stop near the gate!
Why, did the bus stop near the gate.
questions.correctAnswer: Why did the bus stop near the gate?
questions.explanation: A direct question should end with a question mark and have clear word order.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate direct questions correctly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a misplaced modifier?
options: Running quickly, the bag fell from Juma's hand.
Running quickly, Juma dropped the bag.
Juma dropped the bag while running quickly.
As Juma ran quickly, the bag fell.
questions.correctAnswer: Running quickly, the bag fell from Juma's hand.
questions.explanation: The sentence wrongly suggests the bag was running quickly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sentences where describing phrases are placed incorrectly.

questions.prompt: Which option best joins these sentences without repeating words: The mango was ripe. The mango was sweet.
options: The mango was ripe and sweet.
The mango was ripe the mango was sweet.
The mango was ripe because sweet.
questions.correctAnswer: The mango was ripe and sweet.
questions.explanation: And joins the two describing words smoothly without repeating the subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine short sentences to improve fluency.

questions.prompt: Read the sentence: The matatu crawled through the traffic. What does crawled suggest here?
options: It moved very quietly under water.
questions.correctAnswer: It moved very slowly.
questions.explanation: Crawled is used figuratively to show slow movement through traffic.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret figurative word meanings from context.

questions.prompt: Which option shows the correct order for writing a simple composition?
options: plan ideas, write a draft, revise and edit
edit first, forget the topic, then plan
write the final copy, then choose a topic
revise, plan, then remove all ideas
questions.correctAnswer: plan ideas, write a draft, revise and edit
questions.explanation: Good writing usually begins with planning, then drafting, revising and editing.
questions.learningOutcome: Follow stages of the writing process.

questions.prompt: Read the passage: Our debate team lost the first round, but we listened to advice, researched more facts and spoke with confidence in the next round. What is the main lesson?
options: Improvement comes through practice and learning from feedback.
Debates are won by arriving late.
Research is not useful in speaking.
questions.correctAnswer: Improvement comes through practice and learning from feedback.
questions.explanation: The team improved after listening, preparing and speaking better.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer the lesson or theme of a short text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best improves this weak sentence: The day was nice.
options: The cool morning breeze made the sports day pleasant.
questions.correctAnswer: The cool morning breeze made the sports day pleasant.
questions.explanation: The improved sentence gives clear details instead of using the vague word nice.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise vague sentences by adding precise details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best removes unnecessary repetition?
options: The learners cleaned the hall and arranged the chairs.
The learners cleaned the hall and the learners arranged the chairs.
The learners cleaned cleaned the hall.
The learners arranged the chairs and arranged the chairs.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners cleaned the hall and arranged the chairs.
questions.explanation: The sentence keeps both actions but avoids repeating the subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Edit sentences to remove unnecessary repetition.

questions.prompt: Which transition word best completes the paragraph: We washed the vegetables. ____, we chopped them for the stew.
questions.correctAnswer: Next
questions.explanation: Next shows the following step in a sequence.
questions.learningOutcome: Use transition words to connect ideas in order.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best supports the topic sentence: Reading every day improves language skills?
options: It helps learners learn new words and sentence patterns.
The football pitch is behind the dining hall.
Some desks are made of wood.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps learners learn new words and sentence patterns.
questions.explanation: A supporting sentence should explain or give evidence for the topic sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose relevant supporting details for a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Read the dialogue: Mary: Could you help me carry these books? Ali: Of course. Which response would best continue the conversation politely?
options: Thank you, Ali. I appreciate your help.
Move away; I do not need you.
Why are you standing there silently?
questions.correctAnswer: Thank you, Ali. I appreciate your help.
questions.explanation: A polite conversation continues with thanks when someone offers help.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond appropriately and politely in conversations.

questions.prompt: Which question would help you find the main reason for poor attendance at club meetings?
options: Why have some members stopped attending meetings?
What colour is the club noticeboard?
How many windows are in the classroom?
Which pen did the secretary use?
questions.correctAnswer: Why have some members stopped attending meetings?
questions.explanation: A why question asks for reasons and would help identify the cause.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask purposeful questions to gather information.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes this statement into a polite request: Open the window.
options: Could you please open the window?
Open the window now or leave.
questions.correctAnswer: Could you please open the window?
questions.explanation: Could you please makes the request respectful.
questions.learningOutcome: Transform commands into polite requests.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a contrast connector?
options: The story was long, yet it remained interesting.
The story was long because it was long.
The story was long and long.
questions.correctAnswer: The story was long, yet it remained interesting.
questions.explanation: Yet connects two contrasting ideas: long but still interesting.
questions.learningOutcome: Use connectors to show contrast between ideas.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains why the sentence is unclear: After feeding the calf, the gate was closed.
options: It sounds as if the gate fed the calf.
It has no punctuation at all.
It is written as a question.
questions.correctAnswer: It sounds as if the gate fed the calf.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase should clearly describe the person who fed the calf.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how misplaced phrases affect meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines cause and effect?
options: Because the path was muddy, we walked carefully.
The path was muddy and blue pencils.
questions.correctAnswer: Because the path was muddy, we walked carefully.
questions.explanation: The sentence clearly links the muddy path to the careful walking.
questions.learningOutcome: Use subordinating conjunctions to show cause and effect.

questions.prompt: Read the passage: At first, Sifa feared speaking before the class. She practised with her group each lunch break. On Friday, she presented clearly and smiled. What changed?
options: Sifa became more confident through practice.
Sifa made her group practise less.
questions.correctAnswer: Sifa became more confident through practice.
questions.explanation: The passage shows that practice helped Sifa speak clearly and confidently.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how a character changes across a short text.

questions.prompt: Which option best identifies the author's purpose in a text that explains how to make a compost pit?
options: to instruct readers on a process
to invite readers to a birthday party
to entertain with a fairy tale
questions.correctAnswer: to instruct readers on a process
questions.explanation: A text explaining how to make something gives instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the purpose of different informational texts.

questions.prompt: Which detail would be least useful in a report about a class trip to the museum?
questions.correctAnswer: the writer's shoe size
questions.explanation: A shoe size does not help readers understand the trip.
questions.learningOutcome: Select relevant details for a short report.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a formal tone suitable for writing to the head teacher?
options: I kindly request permission to use the hall for debate practice.
Hey, give us the hall today.
Let us grab that hall now.
questions.correctAnswer: I kindly request permission to use the hall for debate practice.
questions.explanation: Formal writing uses respectful and clear language.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal tone in official communication.

questions.prompt: Which option best revises the fragment: When the bell rang.
options: When the bell rang, the pupils lined up.
When rang the bell the pupils.
questions.correctAnswer: When the bell rang, the pupils lined up.
questions.explanation: The revision adds a complete main idea to the dependent clause.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentence fragments into complete sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly with an introductory phrase?
options: After the game, we congratulated the winning team.
After, the game we congratulated the winning team.
After the game we, congratulated the winning team.
After the game we congratulated, the winning team.
questions.correctAnswer: After the game, we congratulated the winning team.
questions.explanation: A comma after the introductory phrase helps separate it from the main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas after introductory phrases.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best shows a balanced opinion for a class discussion?
options: School uniforms are useful, but learners should also keep them neat and comfortable.
Uniforms are bad and nobody should talk.
questions.correctAnswer: School uniforms are useful, but learners should also keep them neat and comfortable.
questions.explanation: A balanced opinion gives a clear view while considering another important point.
questions.learningOutcome: Express opinions respectfully with supporting ideas.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a synonym to avoid repeating the word small?
options: The small seed grew into a tiny shoot.
The small seed grew into a small small shoot.
The seed was small because small.
questions.correctAnswer: The small seed grew into a tiny shoot.
questions.explanation: Tiny is a synonym for small and helps reduce repetition.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve sentences by choosing varied vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best corrects the run-on sentence: We reached the field the match had started?
options: We reached the field after the match had started.
We reached the field the match had started.
The match had started we reached the field.
We reached the field had started the match.
questions.correctAnswer: We reached the field after the match had started.
questions.explanation: After links the two ideas clearly and removes the run-on structure.
questions.learningOutcome: Correct run-on sentences using suitable connectors.

questions.prompt: Read the passage: Amina wanted to win the spelling contest. Instead of only memorising words, she studied word roots, practised pronunciation and asked friends to test her. Which strategy helped her most?
options: using several study methods to understand words
waiting for luck on contest day
questions.correctAnswer: using several study methods to understand words
questions.explanation: Amina combined root study, pronunciation and practice, which supports deeper learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate strategies used by a character in a short passage.

questions.prompt: Which thesis sentence is strongest for a composition about keeping the school clean?
options: Learners can keep the school clean by using bins, joining clean-up teams and caring for shared spaces.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners can keep the school clean by using bins, joining clean-up teams and caring for shared spaces.
questions.explanation: A strong thesis gives a clear main idea and points that can be developed.
